statement: Direct mode is used only when the user explicitly requests it and the work has one clear owning repository.

clear owning repository:

  for the owning task before editing.
- Reconcile existing workers and preserved worktrees before editing; never
  duplicate or race work already in progress.
- Claim or create the owning td task, then implement TDD-first in the requested
  checkout or an isolated worktree.

  branch before the first implementation change.

  gate exactly as a dispatched worker would.

  threads, and merge authorization before calling delivery complete.
- Record handoff, PR, merge, deployment, and cleanup outcomes.

statement: Every dispatched implementation, independent review, PR description, successor, recovery, and final shipping gate must use the same canonical intent revision from `.sergeant-intent.md`.

recovery, and final shipping gate must use the same canonical intent revision from

changes HEAD still requires independent rereview before updating the readiness
marker, but must not trigger repeated no-mistakes review cycles.

source.quote: Deduplication is scoped to the owning repo, axis, source, finding id, parent mission, and branch, so two sessions cannot collide on a generic finding id such as `spec-1`. An update never replaces a stored card: each revision the router writes ends with a `Revision block digest:` line over its own bytes, so a later route can tell whether the stored revision is still exactly what the router wrote. Remove that label once a human has merged the two accounts of the finding; nothing else clears it. A closed card matching a finding is always reopened rather than abandoned, and the reopen is always reported.

statement: Workers always run as persistent interactive TTY sessions; Sergeant never starts one-shot run, prompt, print, or automatic modes.

source.quote:
Workers always run as persistent
interactive TTY sessions. Sergeant never starts one-shot run, prompt, print, or
automatic modes. The base invocation is OpenCode with
`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, Goose with `goose session`, and Claude with no
prompt arguments; when a tuple is pinned, that base is extended with the
harness's own measured model transport — argv for OpenCode, plus `--agent`
against a generated definition when a variant is pinned, and
`GOOSE_PROVIDER`/`GOOSE_MODEL` in the environment for Goose. Initial briefs
and later responses remain in durable files. A worker-owned loop retries only a
fixed ID-bearing terminal nudge until the agent acknowledges that ID before
acting, so delayed TUI startup and coordinator crashes do not lose or duplicate
the mission, and no body appears in process arguments.

trigger: a worker is launched by dispatch
outcome: only persistent interactive sessions are ever started

statement: OpenCode workers are launched with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` because workers run in an automated dispatch context (no operator at the keyboard) and operator trust is scoped at dispatch time by the reviewed intent file and worker brief, which bound what the agent may do.

source.quote:
OpenCode is launched with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in every Sergeant
worker. This is intentional and the rationale is:

- Workers run in an **automated dispatch context**, not an interactive session.
  The operator is not at the keyboard and cannot respond to individual
  permission prompts.
- **Operator trust is scoped at dispatch time**: the intent file and worker
  brief reviewed and approved before dispatch define the boundaries of the work.
  The agent cannot escalate beyond that scope.

trigger: an OpenCode worker is dispatched
outcome: the interactive permission UI is bypassed, with trust instead enforced by the pre-approved intent/brief boundary

statement: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is not a capability grant; the actual trust boundary is the intent file content approved at dispatch time, the worker brief injected into the session, and the repository permissions of the worktree the worker checks out into.

source.quote:
The flag is not a capability grant — it is a bypass of the interactive
confirmation UI. The actual trust boundary is the intent file content approved
at dispatch time, the worker brief injected into the session, and the repository
permissions of the worktree the worker checks out into.

trigger: a worker runs with the interactive permission UI bypassed
outcome: the real authorization boundary remains the reviewed intent/brief/repo-permissions, not the bypass flag itself
notes: Consequence-class: safety/human-decision — clarifies what the bypass does NOT authorize, next to what it does.

notes: Consequence-class: safety — a precondition gate (validated intent file) required before dispatch is allowed to mutate anything, specifically for security-sensitive categories of work.

outcome: panes are stopped only after identity verification, and ambiguous interrupted records wait out a grace period before being marked failed
notes: Consequence-class: identity/recovery — pane stop requires identity verification; an ambiguous interrupted state is not immediately declared failed.

statement: A condition that can no longer be met converts the worker to `needs_input` with the remedy in `.sergeant-message` instead of retrying until its deadline — covering a named check that concluded unsuccessfully, a check absent from an already-completed run, an ambiguous duplicate check name, or a condition missing a required field.

forever; add the field and resume with `sgt-respond`.

blocks the wait rather than being silently counted as drained.

the intent through `--intent`, accepting the exposure. Consent is a flag rather
than an environment variable so it cannot be exported once and silently reapplied
to later runs.

trigger: an operator explicitly wants to allow argv-based intent transport
outcome: the exposure-accepting consent applies to exactly one invocation and cannot silently persist
notes: Consequence-class: human-decision/safety — consent for the riskier transport is scoped to a single explicit invocation, never a silently-persisting override.

statement: The transport actually launched is recorded twice — `validation_intent_transport` for the current run (cleared on retry-reset) and an append-only owner-only `validation_transport.log` of every committed launch — and the validation worker re-checks the recorded transport against the build that will actually run, so a no-mistakes binary replaced between launch and run can neither downgrade the private transport into argv nor invoke a flag that build rejects.

source.quote:
The transport actually launched is recorded twice: `validation_intent_transport`
holds it for the current run and is cleared when a finished run is reset for a
retry, and `validation_transport.log` appends the timestamp, transport, HEAD, and
intent revision of every committed launch so the privacy decision stays auditable
across retries. Both are owner-only. The validation worker re-checks the recorded
transport against the build that will actually run, so a no-mistakes replaced
between launch and run can neither downgrade the private transport into argv nor
invoke a flag that build rejects.

trigger: a validation run is launched with a chosen transport
outcome: the transport choice is durably auditable, and the build actually executing is re-verified against the recorded choice before running
notes: Consequence-class: identity/safety — the running build is re-verified against the recorded transport decision at execution time, not just trusted at launch time, guarding against a swapped binary.

statement: Validation ownership belongs to the dispatching tmux pane; a coordinator in any other pane must claim ownership explicitly, and a claim is accepted only when the claiming pane proves it really runs inside the pane it names by walking its own process ancestry — a caller that merely exports `TMUX_PANE` cannot satisfy this — and the prior owner must be takeover-eligible (dead/absent pane, mismatched recorded identity, or explicit release) with a live unreleased owner never displaced.

source.quote:
Validation is owned by the tmux pane that dispatched the task. A coordinator in
any other pane - a new session, a restarted client, a replacement coordinator -
must take ownership explicitly:

```bash
sgt-validate <fleet-task-id> <repo> --claim-ownership
sgt-validate <fleet-task-id> <repo> --release-ownership
```

A claim is accepted only when the claiming pane proves it really runs inside the
pane it names, by walking its own process ancestry to that pane's process. A
caller that merely exports `TMUX_PANE` cannot satisfy this. The prior owner must
also be takeover-eligible: its pane is dead or absent, its recorded identity no
longer matches the live pane, or it released ownership with
`--release-ownership` from its own pane. A live, unreleased owner is never
displaced.

trigger: a coordinator other than the original dispatcher needs to claim validation ownership
outcome: ownership transfer requires cryptographic-strength process-ancestry proof of pane identity, and never displaces a live legitimate owner
notes: Consequence-class: identity/safety — process-ancestry proof (not a spoofable env var) is required to claim ownership; a live owner can never be displaced.

statement: Every ownership transfer appends the timestamp, reason, repository, prior and new pane, and both identity tuples to an owner-only `coordinator_handover.log`; a release is consumed by the claim that uses it, so it cannot be replayed later by a third pane.

source.quote:
Every transfer appends the timestamp, reason, repository, prior and new pane, and
both identity tuples to an owner-only `coordinator_handover.log` in the task's
fleet directory. A release is consumed by the claim that uses it, so it cannot be
replayed later by a third pane. Each precondition failure - unset `TMUX_PANE`, a

trigger: an ownership claim/release occurs
outcome: every transfer is durably logged, and a release token is single-use, not replayable
notes: Consequence-class: identity/delivery — a release is single-use (consumed by the claim), preventing replay by an unrelated third pane.

statement: If launch fails before the validation child commits the release, Sergeant rolls back only the checkout, pane, temp files, and fleet-state markers that the current invocation both created and can still prove it owns, preserving preexisting state, reused panes, dangling paths, and concurrent replacements; after the recorded pane and process group have fully exited, rerunning `sgt-validate` safely resets only identity-matched finished state and retries.

source.quote:
If launch fails before the validation child commits the release, Sergeant rolls
back only the checkout, pane, temp files, and fleet-state markers that the
current invocation both created and can still prove it owns. Preexisting state,
reused panes, dangling paths, and concurrent replacements are preserved. After
the recorded validation pane and process group have fully exited, rerunning
`sgt-validate` safely resets only identity-matched finished state and retries
the launch.

trigger: a validation launch fails before commit
outcome: rollback is scoped strictly to provably-owned artifacts of this invocation, never touching state it cannot prove it created
notes: Consequence-class: safety/identity — rollback is scoped to only provably-owned state, protecting concurrent/preexisting state from being clobbered.

statement: Validation is treated as validation-only: each actionable finding is routed into separate, deduplicated owning-repository td work, source is never modified inside the retained validation run, and high-risk findings are escalated rather than approved.

source.quote:
Treat the run as validation-only. Route each actionable finding into separate,
deduplicated owning-repository td work. Do not modify source inside the retained
validation run. Approve low/medium-risk gates and merge passing PRs under
recorded authorization; escalate high-risk findings.

trigger: a validation run surfaces findings
outcome: source is never mutated by the validation run, and only low/medium-risk gates may be approved directly
notes: Consequence-class: safety/human-decision — the validation run's authorization boundary excludes source mutation; high-risk findings escalate rather than being approved by the coordinator.

statement: Cleanup requires terminal/reconciled state, configured cleanup-owner proof for the repository/worktree or treehouse lease, preserved evidence, explicit cleanup-phase proof when replaying an interrupted removal or reconciling an already-absent worktree, fully acknowledged response transport, and no uncommitted or in-use worktree state; cleanup is never used to resolve a waiting, blocked, or orphaned worker.

source.quote:
Cleanup requires terminal/reconciled state, configured cleanup-owner proof for
the repository/worktree or treehouse lease, preserved evidence, explicit
cleanup-phase proof when replaying an interrupted removal or reconciling an
already-absent worktree, fully acknowledged response transport, and no
uncommitted or in-use worktree state. Never use cleanup to resolve a waiting,
blocked, or orphaned worker.

trigger: sgt-cleanup is invoked for a task
outcome: cleanup proceeds only once every named precondition holds, and never as a shortcut for a nonterminal worker state
notes: Consequence-class: safety/recovery — a battery of preconditions (terminal state, owner proof, preserved evidence, no in-use worktree) gates a destructive/irreversible cleanup action; nonterminal states are explicitly barred from being 'resolved' by cleanup.

statement: Supported Sergeant commands are used before manual process, tmux, Git, or fleet-file operations, and exact errors and state are preserved before recovery.

source.quote:
Use supported Sergeant commands before manual process, tmux, Git, or fleet-file
operations. Preserve exact errors and state before recovery.

trigger: a failure is being diagnosed
outcome: supported commands are exhausted first, and evidence is preserved before any recovery attempt
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — evidence is preserved before recovery is attempted.

statement: If another executable named `td` is first on PATH, PATH is corrected rather than wrapping unsupported output indefinitely; `td create --help` must show `--description`, `--json`, and `--work-dir`.

source.quote:
If another executable named `td` is first on PATH, correct PATH rather than
wrapping unsupported output indefinitely. `td create --help` must show
`--description`, `--json`, and `--work-dir`.

trigger: the td on PATH does not support the required flags
outcome: the fix is to correct PATH to the required implementation, not build a wrapper around the wrong one
notes: Consequence-class: identity — the fix targets restoring the correct executable identity on PATH, not working around a wrong one.

statement: A live parent process is insufficient evidence of progress; `in_progress` plus a `live worker stalled` diagnostic is still nonterminal and must be reconciled through the progress rules before killing or relaunching anything, preserving worktree/branch/task/response-generation/handoff first, and using `sgt-recover` only for that exact stall classification.

source.quote:
A live parent process is insufficient. `in_progress` plus a `live worker stalled`
diagnostic is still nonterminal; reconcile it through the progress rules in
[`docs/using-sergeant.md`](using-sergeant.md#monitor-work) before killing or
relaunching anything. Preserve the worktree, branch, task, response generation,
and handoff first, then use `sgt-recover <task-id> <repo>` only for that exact
stall classification. If Sergeant refuses because pane identity or unfinished
notification delivery evidence no longer matches, keep the preserved state and
follow the resulting `needs_input` handoff instead of forcing another retry.

trigger: a worker reports in_progress but shows no movement
outcome: diagnosis and preservation happen before any kill/relaunch/recover action, and recovery is scoped to the exact diagnosed case
notes: Consequence-class: safety/recovery — preserves state and forbids kill/relaunch before the stall is properly diagnosed.

statement: If Sergeant refuses recovery because pane identity or unfinished notification delivery evidence no longer matches, the preserved state is kept and the resulting `needs_input` handoff is followed instead of forcing another retry.

source.quote:
stall classification. If Sergeant refuses because pane identity or unfinished
notification delivery evidence no longer matches, keep the preserved state and
follow the resulting `needs_input` handoff instead of forcing another retry.

trigger: sgt-recover refuses due to identity/notification mismatch
outcome: the refusal is respected — no forced retry — and the human-facing handoff path is followed instead
notes: Consequence-class: human-decision/identity — a recovery refusal on identity mismatch is honored, escalating to needs_input rather than being forced.

statement: An expected dependency-blocked exit must remain blocked; it is not an orphan merely because the process ended, so supported response/recovery is used only after reconciling the record, and its worktree is never cleaned.

source.quote:
Read `.sergeant-message`, td handoff, response generation, and worker exit reason.
An expected dependency-blocked exit must remain blocked; it is not an orphan merely
because the process ended. Use supported response/recovery after reconciling the
record, and do not clean its worktree.

scope: diagnosing a worker that became orphaned after blocking
trigger: a blocked worker's process has exited
outcome: the blocked classification is preserved rather than being reclassified as orphaned on process-exit alone, and cleanup is withheld
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — an expected blocked exit is explicitly not reclassified as orphaned.

statement: A pending response is never overwritten; the exact waiting worker is resumed with `sgt-respond` or the caller waits for the current generation to reach a terminal outcome, `sgt-recover` is never used for an active response generation, and if the worker already applied the response with an existing archive entry, the same `sgt-ack-response` command is rerun from the recorded worker pane to finish acknowledgement and cleanup.

source.quote:
Do not overwrite it. Inspect fleet response generation and worker acknowledgement.
Resume the exact waiting worker with `sgt-respond`, or wait for the current
generation to reach a terminal outcome. Do not use `sgt-recover` for an active
response generation; it is only for an `in_progress` worker that still carries
the exact `live worker stalled` diagnostic. If the worker already applied the
response and the archive entry exists, rerun the same
`sgt-ack-response <task> <repo> <response-id>` command from the recorded worker
pane to finish acknowledgement and plaintext cleanup.

trigger: a response generation is already pending for a worker
outcome: the pending response is never clobbered, and the correct convergence path (resume, wait, or rerun ack) is used instead of recover
notes: Consequence-class: delivery/recovery — a pending response is never overwritten; convergence is via rerun, not by force.

statement: A missing pane plus durable blocked/handoff state is classified as waiting work; a missing pane from `in_progress` without a handoff is orphan evidence.

source.quote:
Missing pane plus durable blocked/handoff state is waiting work; missing pane from
`in_progress` without a handoff is orphan evidence.

trigger: a worker's pane cannot be found
outcome: the classification (waiting vs orphan) depends on whether durable handoff state accompanies the missing pane
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — the ambiguous 'pane missing' condition is disambiguated by durable handoff evidence rather than assumed.

statement: Repeated notifications are diagnosed by comparing task, repo, state generation, message digest, and timestamp, since they can indicate stale fleet records, unconsumed responses, or an expected blocked worker incorrectly reclassified orphaned; duplicate tasks or duplicate responses are never created in reaction.

source.quote:
notifications can be stale fleet records, unconsumed responses, or expected blocked
workers incorrectly reclassified orphaned. Do not create duplicate tasks or send
duplicate responses.

trigger: notifications repeat for the same worker
outcome: the underlying cause is diagnosed via a fixed comparison rather than reacting with new duplicate tasks/responses
notes: Consequence-class: delivery — explicitly avoids creating duplicate tasks/responses in reaction to repeated notifications.

statement: An `auto-fix` finding in Sergeant's validation-only workflow is never authorized as an in-run fix; it is instead routed to separate owning-repository td remediation, and a retained gate is never edited, aborted, or restarted to bypass the finding.

source.quote:
- auto-fix: Do not authorize an in-run fix in Sergeant's validation-only
  workflow; route the finding to separate owning-repository td remediation.
- retained gate: do not edit, abort, or restart it to bypass the finding.

trigger: a no-mistakes run is parked with an auto-fix or retained-gate finding
outcome: the finding is routed out-of-run rather than fixed in-run, and gates are never bypassed by editing/aborting/restarting
notes: Consequence-class: safety — a validation-only boundary prohibiting in-run fixes and gate-bypass workarounds.

statement: If shared daemon credentials cannot access one repository, the global GitHub account is never switched while unrelated runs are active; an approved repo-scoped method, waiting, or an explicit manual-shipping override is used instead.

source.quote:
If shared daemon credentials cannot access one repository, do not switch the global
GitHub account while unrelated runs are active. Use an approved repo-scoped method,
wait, or obtain an explicit manual-shipping override.

scope: diagnosing a GitHub access problem during a shared no-mistakes run
trigger: a credential-access problem arises while other runs may be using shared credentials
outcome: the global credential identity is never switched underneath other active runs
notes: Consequence-class: identity/safety — global credential identity is not mutated while other work depends on it.

statement: A one-shot `GH_TOKEN` for `gh` and a one-shot credential helper for Git are preferred, and the global GitHub account is never switched while other workers may invoke GitHub operations.

source.quote:
Prefer one-shot `GH_TOKEN` for `gh` and a one-shot credential helper for Git. Do
not switch the global account while other workers may invoke GitHub operations.

trigger: a repository needs different GitHub credentials than the global default
outcome: scoped one-shot credentials are used instead of a global account switch that could affect concurrent workers
notes: Consequence-class: identity — prefers scoped, non-global credential resolution to avoid disturbing concurrent workers' identity assumptions.

statement: Parsing proof of Bash 3.2 compatibility does not replace runtime proof unless the task acceptance explicitly permits parsing only.

source.quote:
regression, including the `sgt-dispatch` Bash 3.2 parse and branch-name
regression for shipped scripts. Parsing proof does not replace runtime proof
unless the task acceptance explicitly permits parsing only.

trigger: Bash 3.2 compatibility is being verified for shipped scripts
outcome: runtime proof is required by default; parse-only proof is insufficient unless explicitly permitted by task acceptance

statement: Graphify output for a project is kept to one output path outside source repositories, and an existing graph is never regenerated or moved without confirming the desired global-per-project path.

source.quote:
Run `sgt-context <project>` and inspect project-level `graphify.output`. Keep one
output per project outside source repositories. Do not regenerate or move an
existing graph without confirming the desired global-per-project path.

trigger: graphify output looks wrong or recursive
outcome: the output path stays single and outside source repos, and moves/regenerations are confirmed first

statement: Fleet files are never force-deleted or manually edited when cleanup refuses; cleanup safety depends on terminal proof, staged evidence, exact configured repository/worktree/lease identity, explicit cleanup phases for replayed/already-absent cases, proof of completed removal, and a response handshake that is either fully converged or explicitly retired, and cleanup intentionally refuses while any of that is only partially published.

source.quote:
Do not force or delete fleet files manually. Cleanup safety depends on terminal
proof, staged evidence, exact configured repository identity, original
worktree/lease identity, explicit cleanup phases for replayed removals or
already-absent worktrees, proof that a recorded removal actually completed, and a
response handshake that is either fully converged or explicitly retired.
Preserve the worktree and run the owning remediation or supported retry path;
cleanup intentionally refuses while response archive, acknowledgement markers, or
active plaintext transport are only partially published and the handshake could
still be completed.

scope: diagnosing cleanup refusal or partial state
trigger: sgt-cleanup refuses or leaves partial state
outcome: the refusal is honored — no manual force-delete — and the owning remediation/retry path is used instead
notes: Consequence-class: safety — cleanup's refusal to proceed on incomplete evidence is honored rather than manually forced.

statement: `<repo> has pending or incomplete response acknowledgement` means a response was delivered but never acknowledged; the only path that completes the handshake is resuming the worker and acknowledging with `sgt-ack-response` from that worker's own pane.

source.quote:
`<repo> has pending or incomplete response acknowledgement` means a response was
delivered but never acknowledged. Resume the worker and acknowledge it with
`sgt-ack-response` from that worker's own pane; that is the only path that
completes a handshake.

scope: cleanup refusing an unfinished response handshake
trigger: cleanup reports a pending/incomplete response acknowledgement
outcome: completion requires the exact worker's own pane to run sgt-ack-response; no other path completes it
notes: Consequence-class: identity — completion of the handshake requires the exact worker's own pane, not an equivalent substitute.

statement: When the worker is gone for good, cleanup can retire the handshake instead, but only when, re-checked on every attempt, both hold: the owning td task is closed, and the recorded worker is provably dead (pane gone/dead with matching identity, recorded PID not running, no process in its recorded process group, and worker_pid/worker_process_start/worker_process_group all recorded).

source.quote:
When the worker is gone for good, cleanup can retire the handshake instead, but
only when both of these hold, re-checked on every attempt:

- the owning `td` task is **closed**, resolved in that repo's own repository; and
- the recorded worker is **provably dead** — its pane is gone or dead with a
  matching identity, its recorded PID is not running, no process remains in its
  recorded process group, and `worker_pid`, `worker_process_start` and
  `worker_process_group` are all recorded.

trigger: cleanup considers retiring a handshake because the worker appears gone
outcome: retirement requires two independently re-verified conditions (closed owning task, provably dead worker) on every attempt, not a one-time check
notes: Consequence-class: safety/identity — retirement requires provable death (PID/process-group/start-time checked, not just PID existence) re-verified every attempt, guarding against PID reuse.

statement: The refusal names which condition failed (e.g. process still alive, PID reused, pane identity mismatch, owning td task not closed); a live, PID-reused, or identity-mismatched owner is always refused, since it is never correct to retire a handshake underneath a worker that might still finish it.

source.quote:
The refusal names which condition failed, for example `recorded worker process
<pid> is still alive`, `recorded worker PID <pid> was reused`, `recorded worker
pane identity does not match`, or `owning td task is in_progress, not closed`. A
live, PID-reused, or identity-mismatched owner is always refused: it is never
correct to retire a handshake underneath a worker that might still finish it.

trigger: a retirement attempt fails one of the death/closure conditions
outcome: retirement is refused with a named cause whenever the worker might still be alive or its identity is ambiguous
notes: Consequence-class: safety — a PID-reused or identity-mismatched owner explicitly blocks retirement, guarding against acting under a live worker.

statement: Retirement records the exact partial state under `~/.local/share/sergeant/fleet/<task>/<repo>/response-retirement/` before mutating anything (verbatim copies of both sides, owner death evidence, and provable response-archive fields), never writes an acknowledgement, and marks a `retired` directory so the archive can never be read as one; the archive shares the fleet task's lifetime so a retried cleanup converges.

source.quote:
Retirement records the exact partial state under
`~/.local/share/sergeant/fleet/<task>/<repo>/response-retirement/` before it
mutates anything — verbatim copies of both sides under `partial/`, the owner death
evidence in `owner`, and the response-archive fields it can prove. It never writes
an acknowledgement, and the `retired` marker in that directory means the archive
can never be read as one. The archive has the same lifetime as the fleet task's
`response-archive`: it exists so a retried cleanup converges, and it is removed
with the rest of the fleet state, so capture it before a successful run if you
need it. A retirement prints `retiring unfinishable response handshake: <repo>
response=<id> generation=<n> owner_pid=<pid>` in the cleanup output.

trigger: a retirement proceeds after both conditions are verified
outcome: the retirement is durably recorded before any mutation, is distinguishable from a real acknowledgement, and remains available for a retried cleanup to converge against
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — a durable record is published before the destructive retirement mutates state, so a retried cleanup can converge.

statement: Cleanup refuses a retirement archive that no longer describes the state it preserved — a changed response, a tampered or symlinked copy, or a drifted recorded owner — rather than trusting stale evidence.

source.quote:
Cleanup refuses a retirement archive that no longer describes the state it
preserved — including a changed response, a tampered or symlinked copy, and a
recorded owner that has drifted — rather than trusting stale evidence.

scope: retiring an unfinishable response handshake, re-verification
trigger: a retirement archive is consulted on a later cleanup attempt
outcome: the archive is re-validated against current reality before being trusted, and refused if it no longer matches
notes: Consequence-class: safety/identity — a previously-recorded retirement archive is re-validated, not blindly trusted, before being relied on again.

statement: `sgt-cleanup` requires fleet state and worktree to be on the same filesystem because it uses atomic rename operations to move and restore evidence during terminal worker removal, and atomic rename does not cross filesystems; Sergeant refuses cross-filesystem layouts rather than falling back to a non-atomic copy+delete that could leave evidence in an inconsistent state.

source.quote:
This is a deliberate constraint, not a bug. `sgt-cleanup` uses atomic rename operations
to safely move and restore evidence during terminal worker removal. Atomic rename only
works within a single filesystem (`EXDEV` on rename across devices). Sergeant therefore
refuses cross-filesystem layouts rather than falling back to a non-atomic copy+delete
that could leave evidence in an inconsistent state.

trigger: SERGEANT_FLEET and a project worktree are on different filesystems
outcome: cleanup refuses the cross-filesystem layout rather than risking an inconsistent-evidence fallback
notes: Consequence-class: safety/recovery — refuses a non-atomic fallback that could leave evidence in an inconsistent state; fails closed instead.

statement: When documentation does not cover an observed failure, the `sergeant-help` skill is used to search the docs, then a td task is created containing the exact reproduction, expected behavior, preserved state, and acceptance criteria.

source.quote:
If documentation does not cover the observed failure, use the `sergeant-help`
skill to search the docs, then create a td task containing the exact reproduction,
expected behavior, preserved state, and acceptance criteria.

trigger: a failure is not covered by existing documentation
outcome: the gap is escalated as a well-formed td task rather than left unresolved or guessed at

statement: Repo `path` values that are not absolute or home-relative are resolved relative to `dev_root`, so project YAMLs stay portable across machines by changing `dev_root` in one place.

source.quote: All scripts read `dev_root` at startup. Repo `path` values that are not absolute (`/...`) or home-relative (`~/...`) are resolved relative to `dev_root`. This makes project YAMLs portable across machines — change `dev_root` in one place instead of every path in every YAML.

trigger: a repo path is resolved
outcome: relative paths resolve against a single configured root rather than being hardcoded per-YAML
authority: sgt-context / any sgt-* script reading project YAML

statement: Durable callback implementations are executable profiles under `~/.config/sergeant/callbacks/`; they are not project YAML fields, and fleet requests cannot supply paths.

source.quote:
Durable callback implementations are executable profiles under
`~/.config/sergeant/callbacks/`; they are not project YAML fields and fleet
requests cannot supply paths. See [Durable Callback Protocol](callbacks.md) for
the profile ownership/mode rules and versioned consumer schema.

trigger: a callback profile is referenced by a fleet request
outcome: the executable profile path is never taken from a fleet request, only from the fixed local callbacks directory
notes: Consequence-class: safety — a fleet-supplied path can never select which executable profile runs; the profile location is fixed and out-of-band from request input.

statement: A project's `name` field must match its filename.

source.quote: | `name` | string | yes | Project identifier. Must match the filename. |

trigger: a project YAML is loaded
outcome: name/filename mismatch is a validation condition

statement: A repo's `name` must match `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`, cannot contain spaces, and cannot be `.` or `..`, so Sergeant can safely prefix merged source paths with it for `sgt-graphify`.

source.quote: | `name` | string | yes | Short identifier for this repo. Used in output and context blocks. For `sgt-graphify`, it must match `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`, cannot contain spaces, and cannot be `.` or `..`, so Sergeant can safely prefix merged source paths with it. |

trigger: a repo entry's name is used to prefix merged graphify source paths
outcome: an unsafe repo name (path-traversal-shaped or space-containing) is rejected by this constraint before being used as a path prefix
notes: Consequence-class: safety — the name constraint (rejecting '.', '..', spaces) exists specifically to make prefixing merged paths with it safe, i.e. guards against path-traversal-shaped names.

statement: GitHub CLI identity for dispatch resolves in strict precedence: `repo.identity` → `project.identity` → `config.default_identity` → no-op.

source.quote: | `identity` | string | no | GitHub CLI user for `gh auth switch` before dispatching this repo. Overrides project-level `identity` and `config.default_identity`. Resolution order: `repo.identity` → `project.identity` → `config.default_identity` → no-op. |

trigger: a repo is about to be dispatched to
outcome: the identity used is deterministically the first defined value in this fixed precedence chain
notes: Consequence-class: identity — a fixed, explicit precedence chain for which credential identity is active, never ambiguous.

statement: If `graphify.output` is a directory symlink, `sgt-graphify` preserves the symlink and publishes into its target; Sergeant only replaces the published graph after a complete run and preserves existing `wiki/` and `memory/` directories.

source.quote: | `output` | string | yes | Published output directory for the merged project graph. A trailing `/` is allowed. If this path is a directory symlink, `sgt-graphify` preserves the symlink and publishes into its target. Sergeant only replaces the published graph after a complete run and preserves existing `wiki/` and `memory/` directories. |

trigger: sgt-graphify publishes its output
outcome: publication is atomic-after-completion and never destroys the wiki/memory subdirectories or an existing symlink structure
notes: Consequence-class: delivery — the published graph is only replaced after a complete run (not partially/incrementally), an exactly-once-per-run publish guarantee.

statement: If `graphify.output` lives inside a source repo, Sergeant stages extraction outside that repo and excludes the configured output path, so published graph artifacts are never re-ingested as source.

source.quote: | `exclude_patterns` | list | no | Glob patterns to exclude from graphify traversal (e.g., `**/node_modules/**`). Sergeant applies them before `graphify extract`, so they keep working with current Graphify CLIs that do not accept exclude flags. If `graphify.output` lives inside a source repo, Sergeant stages extraction outside that repo and excludes the configured output path so published graph artifacts are never re-ingested as source. |

trigger: graphify.output is configured inside a source repo
outcome: the published graph never becomes an input to its own next extraction
notes: Consequence-class: safety — prevents an unbounded self-ingestion loop by excluding the output path from its own extraction.

statement: Agent instruction layers are concatenated in order (defaults, group, repo) with later layers appearing later in the block, and when directives conflict the later, more specific repository-level directive is the intended authority; Sergeant does not structurally merge or deduplicate the free-form prose.

source.quote:
`sgt-context` emits every nonempty layer in one block. Later layers appear later
in the block; when directives conflict, the later repository-specific directive
is the intended authority. Sergeant does not structurally merge or deduplicate
free-form instruction prose, but `sgt-dispatch` still classifies review routing
from a single normalized in-memory context built from the mission, repo role,
repo group name, repo group description, and merged default/group/repository
instructions.

trigger: sgt-context assembles instructions for a repo
outcome: conflict resolution between layers is by position/specificity (later/repo wins), not automatic merging

statement: A project's `dag.name` must be unique across all projects known to `dagr`, since `sgt-dag-run` runs it as a DAG identified by that name.

source.quote:
dag:
  name: myapp-delivery           # DAG name in dagr (must be unique across all projects)

trigger: a project declares a dag block and sgt-dag-run is used
outcome: the dag name must not collide with any other project's dag name
notes: Consequence-class: identity — the dag name is a cross-project identifier that must be unique, not merely unique within the project.

statement: Each DAG stage names the repos it dispatches to and pulls its brief from a td task via `td:`, or from an explicit inline `brief:` when `td:` is not set.

source.quote:
- name: foundation            # stage name (unique within this dag)
      repos: [myapp-api]          # repos to dispatch to

statement: The Docker drain test suite runs the same test file in two passes — system Bash under Debian bookworm-slim, and Bash 3.2 under an official Alpine bash:3.2 image — and reports overall pass/fail only once both passes are accounted for.

source.quote:
[tasks."test:docker:drain"]
description = "Run the drain test suite in Docker (system Bash + Bash 3.2 passes)"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs the drain test suite in two Docker passes:
#
#   Pass 1 — Debian bookworm-slim (system Bash 5.x)
#     Tests drain state helpers, sgt-drain --status (bug #82), drain lock
#     functions (bug #81), and sgt-recover drain gating.
#
#   Pass 2 — bash:3.2 Alpine image
#     Re-runs the same tests under Bash 3.2 to confirm Bash 3.2 compatibility.
#
# Prerequisites: Docker must be available.  The test image is built locally and
# not pushed; the bash:3.2 image is pulled from Docker Hub on first use.

set -euo pipefail
REPO_DIR="$(git -C "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT:-.}" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

SGT_BASH32_IMAGE="docker.io/library/bash:3.2@sha256:3a13e5da38baa575985778cd09ce8ac736d4b4dafc91a430e71271f6e5311b89"

pass=0
fail=0

_docker_pass() {
  local label="$1" image="$2" cmd="$3"
  printf '\\n══ %s ══\\n' "$label"
  if docker run --rm -v "${REPO_DIR}:/repo:ro" "$image" sh -c "$cmd"; then
    printf '\\n✓  %s passed\\n' "$label"
    pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    printf '\\n✗  %s FAILED\\n' "$label" >&2
    fail=$((fail + 1))
  fi
}

# Build the Debian test image (cached after first build).
printf 'Building sergeant-test image...\\n'
docker build -q -f "${REPO_DIR}/Dockerfile.test" -t sergeant-test "${REPO_DIR}"
printf 'Built.\\n'

# Pass 1: system Bash (Debian bookworm-slim).
_docker_pass "System Bash (Debian bookworm-slim)" \
  sergeant-test \
  "BASH32='' bash /repo/tests/run-drain-tests.sh"

# Pass 2: Bash 3.2 (official Alpine image).
# Sets BASH32 to the Alpine Bash binary path and SGT_MINIMUM_BASH for the
# runtime-bash-test compatibility check.
_docker_pass "Bash 3.2 (Alpine)" \
  "$SGT_BASH32_IMAGE" \
  "BASH32=/usr/local/bin/bash SGT_MINIMUM_BASH=/usr/local/bin/bash bash /repo/tests/run-drain-tests.sh"

printf '\\n═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\\n'
printf ' Docker drain suite: %d passed, %d failed\\n' "$pass" "$fail"
printf '═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\\n'
[[ $fail -eq 0 ]]
"""

notes: Consequence-class: identity — a single source of truth is used specifically because two independently-maintained copies of the same contract previously drifted and caused an operational failure (workers hand-creating cards instead of routing).

statement: Only the canonical `error` severity family publishes a blocking review gate; `high` is deliberately treated as must-fix (mapped to `error`) so a genuinely blocking finding can never ship as mere debt.

source.quote:
# Owner decision on td-61a0c8 (Option A): the canonical set is error|warning|info
# and `informational` is no longer a first-class severity. The decision turned on
# which severities halt a worker, not on spelling, so the reviewer spellings that
# reviewers actually emit are accepted and normalized instead of failing a whole
# axis on a vocabulary mismatch. Only the `error` family publishes a blocking
# gate: "high" is treated as must-fix so a genuinely blocking finding cannot ship
# as debt. Narrowing the canonical set satisfies td-efe124; documenting it in the
# usage text and the generated contract satisfies td-c09980.

trigger: a reviewer reports a finding with severity `high`
outcome: a finding severe enough to be called high is guaranteed to block, never silently downgraded to nonblocking debt
notes: Consequence-class: safety — a specific severity spelling (high) is deliberately pinned to the blocking tier so it can never be misclassified as mere debt.

statement: `.sergeant-intent.md`'s revision is never silently regenerated by the worker; only an audited human decision creates a new intent revision, and successor/recovery work must inherit the exact existing revision.

source.quote: .sergeant-intent.md is the canonical source for implementation decisions, independent reviews, PR description, and the one final no-mistakes --intent. Intent revision: {{INTENT_REVISION}}. Successor and recovery work must inherit this exact revision. Do not silently regenerate it; only an audited human decision creates a new intent revision.

trigger: a worker considers whether the canonical intent needs to change
outcome: the intent revision's identity is stable unless a human explicitly re-authors it, even across successor/recovery work
notes: Consequence-class: identity/human-decision — the canonical intent revision can only change via an audited human decision, never a worker's own silent regeneration, and must be honored exactly by successor/recovery work.

statement: Non-interactive agent launch modes are prohibited for a worker: it never launches `opencode run`, `goose run`, Claude print mode, `--auto`, `--prompt`, or an equivalent one-shot mode, since Sergeant delivers only a fixed ID-bearing notification through interactive terminal input.

source.quote: Your worker runs as a persistent interactive agent session in its recorded tmux pane. Non-interactive agent modes are prohibited: do not launch `opencode run`, `goose run`, Claude print mode, `--auto`, `--prompt`, or an equivalent one-shot agent. Sergeant delivers only a fixed ID-bearing notification through interactive terminal input; prompt, response, and secret bodies remain in durable files and never appear in process arguments.

trigger: a worker is running its session
outcome: the worker session stays interactive and persistent, never switching to a one-shot non-interactive mode
notes: Consequence-class: safety — a worker is explicitly barred from switching itself into a one-shot/non-interactive mode, preserving the interactive notification delivery contract.

statement: A worker follows a notification instruction exactly once per token; repeated nudges carrying the same token are treated as retries, not new work.

source.quote: For every Sergeant notification, read `.sergeant-notification` and copy the exact supervisor-scoped token from the nudge (`notification_id|target_nonce`) to the named file under `.sergeant-notification-acks/`. Do not act until that supervisor sends acceptance and the named file under `.sergeant-notification-accepts/` contains the same token. Then follow the instruction exactly once and write the token to the named file under `.sergeant-notification-complete/`. Repeated nudges with the same token are retries, not new work.

trigger: a worker receives a notification nudge with a token it has already completed
outcome: the same token is never acted on twice, so a retried nudge cannot cause duplicate action
notes: Consequence-class: delivery — a worker treats a same-token repeated nudge as a retry, guaranteeing at-most-once action per token even under redelivery.

statement: If an agent exits before reaching a terminal or waiting state, the supervisor records `orphaned` with durable diagnostics and td recovery pointers; orphaned work is resumed only through `sgt-respond`, and its recovery state is never overwritten or discarded.

source.quote: If an agent exits before a terminal or waiting state, the supervisor records `orphaned` with durable diagnostics and td recovery pointers. Resume orphaned work through `sgt-respond`; do not overwrite or discard its recovery state.

trigger: a worker's agent process exits before a terminal or waiting state
outcome: the resulting orphaned state carries durable, preserved recovery evidence rather than being silently lost or overwritten by a naive restart
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — orphaned recovery state is explicitly preserved (never overwritten/discarded), and resume is channeled through one supported command.

statement: `.sergeant-gate-generation` is a monotonic integer for waiting gates: before every new `needs_input` or `blocked` publication, the worker increments and persists the generation before writing the waiting status and message, so a repeated blocker message only counts as a new gate when the generation actually advances.

source.quote: Maintain `.sergeant-gate-generation` as a monotonic integer for waiting gates. Before every new `needs_input` or `blocked` publication, increment the generation and persist it before writing the waiting status and message. A repeated blocker message is still a new gate only when the generation advances.

trigger: a worker publishes a needs_input or blocked gate
outcome: gate identity is tied to a monotonically advancing generation, published before the status/message it gates, so stale or repeated messages are distinguishable from genuinely new gates
notes: Consequence-class: identity/delivery — the gate generation is persisted before the gated status/message, and only an advanced generation counts as a new gate, preventing a repeated message from being mistaken for (or masking) a new one.

statement: Only the allowlisted wake-condition field names and alphanumeric-safe values are accepted in `.sergeant-wake-condition`; arbitrary shell commands, prompt bodies, response text, tokens, or secrets are never persisted there.

source.quote: Optional fields on any kind: `deadline=<unix_timestamp>` (terminal failure if exceeded), `max_attempts=<int>` (becomes needs_input if exceeded), and `backoff_base=<seconds>` (base retry backoff before jitter). Required field on all conditions: `generation=<int>`. Do not persist arbitrary shell commands, prompt bodies, response text, tokens, or secrets in `.sergeant-wake-condition`; only the above allowlisted field names and alphanumeric-safe values are accepted.

trigger: a worker writes .sergeant-wake-condition
outcome: the wake-condition file can never become a vector for persisting or later executing arbitrary/secret content
notes: Consequence-class: safety — the wake-condition file's field set is a closed allowlist, explicitly excluding arbitrary commands, prompt/response text, tokens, and secrets.

statement: Validation requires a clean worktree at the committed HEAD; readiness evidence is never created from an uncommitted diff, and the branch is committed before readiness is published.

source.quote: Commit the reviewed branch before publishing readiness. Validation requires a clean worktree at that committed HEAD; do not create readiness evidence from an uncommitted diff.

trigger: a worker is about to publish .sergeant-validation-ready
outcome: readiness evidence is always anchored to a real, committed, clean HEAD, never a working-tree diff that could still change
notes: Consequence-class: identity/safety — readiness evidence is pinned to a committed, clean HEAD, never an uncommitted (and thus still-mutable) diff.

statement: The worker never approves a validation gate, routes a finding, or remediates validation output from its own pane; the Sergeant coordinator owns every no-mistakes gate and finding, and the worker resumes only through an explicit Sergeant response tied to that owning work.

source.quote: The Sergeant coordinator owns every no-mistakes gate and finding. Do not approve a validation gate, route a finding, or remediate validation output from this worker pane. Actionable findings become separate deduplicated td work and remediation never runs no-mistakes. Resume this worker only through an explicit Sergeant response tied to that owning work.

trigger: a coordinator-owned no-mistakes validation run is in progress
outcome: the worker's authority explicitly excludes acting on validation gates/findings itself, no matter what it observes
notes: Consequence-class: safety/human-decision — a worker's authorization scope explicitly excludes validation-gate actions, which remain coordinator-owned; a 'never authorizes X' boundary next to the worker's broader grant.

statement: A reviewer's structured JSON finding artifact carries only a fixed field set (`findings`, and per finding `id`/`severity`/`disposition`/`summary`/`evidence`/`paths`/`acceptance_criteria`/`recommendation`); review bodies, prompts, secrets, or credentials are never passed into the artifact, td, or fleet metadata.

source.quote: Require each reviewer to return a structured JSON finding artifact with only: `findings`, and per finding `id`, `severity`, `disposition`, `summary`, `evidence`, `paths`, `acceptance_criteria`, and `recommendation`. Set `severity` to one of the canonical values `{{REVIEW_SEVERITIES}}`; the router also accepts and normalizes these reviewer spellings: {{REVIEW_SEVERITY_ALIAS_TABLE}}. Only the `error` family publishes a blocking gate, so reserve it for must-fix findings; `warning` and `info` route as reviewable debt. Route each axis separately with `sgt-review-findings {{PROJECT}} {{REPO_NAME}} --axis <{{REVIEW_AXES_PIPE}}>`, passing the artifact, axis/source, branch/head, parent td mission, fleet task ID, and worktree. The router deduplicates actionable findings into owning-repository td tasks, publishes blocking state and notification, and prints task IDs and recommended remediation. Cosmetic and false-positive dispositions create no cards. Never pass review bodies, prompts, secrets, or credentials into the artifact, td, or fleet metadata. Treat malformed output or routing failure as blocked; do not continue or leave findings only in worker.log.

scope: worker producing a review finding artifact
trigger: a review axis subagent produces its finding artifact
outcome: the artifact's shape is a closed field set that structurally excludes secret-bearing or raw-body content from ever reaching td/fleet metadata
notes: Consequence-class: safety — the finding artifact's schema is a closed allowlist that structurally excludes secrets/credentials/raw bodies from reaching durable storage.
